lines.text: Meet Paul: Widowed, Retired War-Veteran turned Handy Man. He is the proud leader of the neighborhood watch and always claims to 'know it all'
Paul gets up from a nap seeing the chatter is coming from the TV.

lines.speaker: TV
lines.text: In other news, residents of Marin County should be warned. With the summer heat reaching its peak, we are now on high alert for potential fires.

lines.speaker: TV
lines.text: Please stay vigilant and ensure your homes and properties are safeguarded. Again, it is not a red flag day folks! Make your preperations now instead of later!
There's only so much time to prepare - Your actions will have consequences...choose wisely
Paul rushes around the kitchen quickly making a huge feast for one, once done with breakfast he reads the newspaper mentioning fire warnings approaching red flag day.
Paul goes around his home collecting everything he might need to leave when a fire starts(radio, photo memories, medical supplies, flashlight, etc.)

lines.speaker: Cal Fire
lines.text: A go-bag could contain: Three-day supply of non-perishable food and three gallons of water per person, Prescriptions or special medications, First aid kit, Flashlight and extra batteries, Copies of important documents (birth certificates, passports, etc.)
Go to the front yard or the back yard?
Paul's frontyard is wide and large.  A white picket fence surrounds his large front lawn which has turned yellow since Mary died.

choices.text: Check other parts of the yard

lines.text: Paul gets into his car and backs it into the driveway.

lines.speaker: Cal Fire
lines.text: Parking your car in the driveway facing the street is a good idea. It allows for a quick escape in the event of a fire.
Paul quickly mows the yellowed lawn down and sweeps the clippings up.

lines.speaker: Cal Fire
lines.text: Maintaining a well-trimmed lawn is crucial for wildfire protection as it reduces the amount of readily combustible material, creating a natural firebreak that can slow or stop the spread of wildfires near your home. It is important to NOT do yard work during a red flag day however.
Paul goes over to talk to Aldo

lines.speaker: Aldo
lines.text: Paul The fire is looking really bad. If you want to come with us when the evacuation alert goes out, which it will. please let us know its no issue at all.

lines.speaker: Paul
lines.text: Thank you Aldo but I don't think that will be necessary. I'll let you know.
The backyard is relatively big with trees and a brick wall surrounding it. Paul had a pool installed when he and Mary first moved in.

choices.text: Check other parts of the yard

lines.text: Paul carefully climbs to the roof and begins sawing different parts of the tree causing branches to fall.

lines.speaker: Cal Fire
lines.text: Remove all branches within 10 feet of any chimney or stovepipe outlet as they intrude on your home's defensible zone. Cleaning your yard should ONLY be done on non-red flag days.
Paul quickly scoops several handfuls of leaves out of the gutter and into the plant waste bin below. It quickly fills up

lines.speaker: Paul
lines.text: No wonder the gutter had been flooding last winter

lines.speaker: Cal Fire
lines.text: The accumulation of debris in gutters serves as one of the greatest fire hazards for a standing structure. In the event that embers ignite debris the resulting fire will directly expose the edge of the roof to flames. Dealing with ignitables should ONLY be done on non-red flag days.
Knowing the impending danger of a fire, Paul drops everything to evacuate and walk to his nearest county rendezvous point.

lines.speaker: Cal Fire
lines.text: Being safer than sorry is always the best choice. Please heed evacuation notices and get out as early as possible.
Paul ran out of time and the fire encroached. Paul later had to be rescued by fire crews, something he will forever be embarassed by.

lines.speaker: Cal Fire
lines.text: When fire crews tell you to evacuate, EVACUATE!
